- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, reduce forecast slope and avoid upward momentum; model tends to overcorrect after negative sentiment.
- If forecast shows steady upward trend with no recent dip, check for overshoot — true values often dip sharply after initial spike.
- When sentiment is mildly positive (0.2–0.5), model tends to overestimate; cap forecast growth to 0.5–1.0% per day unless strong catalysts exist.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60), model often fails to recognize it — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) — apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and history shows volatility, model tends to smooth too much — allow 1–2% volatility buffer in forecast.
- If true outcome drops below 55 after 10+ days of forecast growth, reset forecast to 55–58 range and reduce slope by 50% for next 3 days.
